title: Pulseweave tenant-mix load conductor: deterministic throughput signatures & customer acceptance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build Pulseweave: a reproducible, tenant-aware load conductor that synthesizes deterministic throughput signatures for Dedicated capacity contracts. Pulseweave generates tenant-mixed traffic profiles (mix of short-chat, long-completion, embedding, and KV-warmup requests), captures end-to-end tail latency and throughput fidelity, and produces artifacts that customers can use for acceptance signoff. The goal is to deliver repeatable evidence for throughput guarantees and to exercise autoscaling gates and fleet controls under contracted conditions.
motivation: Customers buying Dedicated capacity need evidence that we meet throughput and tail-latency guarantees under realistic tenant mixes and autoscaler behavior. Existing repros are ad-hoc; Pulseweave standardizes profiles, warms KV caches consistently, articulates autoscaler stabilization windows, and outputs audit-ready artifacts for SRE and sales signoff.
acceptance_criteria: Pulseweave runs as a single orchestrator job and can execute at three predefined profiles: baseline, mixed-tenant, and surge-burst.
Generated runs include deterministic seeds and a manifest that lists request templates, tenant weights, KV warmup sequences, and model variants; manifests are human-readable YAML.

End-to-end telemetry is exported to a stable Prometheus namespace and a normalized CSV/JSON evidence bundle (per-run: p50/p90/p99 latencies, qps, error rates, heatmaps of sequence length distribution).
Automated acceptance script (./scripts/customer_acceptance.sh) converts evidence bundle into a one-page acceptance PDF and uploads to a GCS signed URL for customer review.
Pulseweave can simulate autoscaler behavior by driving sustained load and then verifying scaling events (node additions/removals) and ensuring request-level SLOs during stabilization windows.
Tool integrates with console rollouts: it can mark a model variant as "test" and replay against canary nodes to show safe fallback behavior.
Operational runbook added to /docs/runbooks/pulseweave.md describing how to interpret artifacts and remediate common failure modes.
Benchmarks are reproducible locally and in CI (ci/pulseweave-e2e) with a deterministic seed to within +-3% for p50/p90 across repeated runs in the same environment.
SRE and Sales have an onboarding checklist to run a customer acceptance session and sign the throughput attestation.
Performance regressions detected by the run produce an automatic ticket template with diffs against the last golden run.
design_notes: Pulseweave composes three sub-systems: profile generator, request driver, and evidence collector. Profile generator: language-agnostic templates for request types (short prompt, streaming, long-context completion, embedding) with tenant weights. Request driver: Go microservice that forks workers per-tenant bucket, supports deterministic random seeds, supports KV cache warmup sequences and controlled prefix caching. Evidence collector: pulls token and request traces, aggregates kernel-level metrics from node exporters, and correlates with autoscaler events (k8s events + cloud provider autoscaler logs). Key design decisions: (1) deterministic seed at profile level to remove sampling variance for acceptance runs; (2) explicit KV-warmup phase to avoid cold-start noise; (3) synthetic tenant mixing to mirror customer mixes but keep PII-free; (4) configurable autoscaler perturbations to validate safety thresholds.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for profile loader and deterministic RNG. 2) Integration test that runs a 10-minute baseline profile in CI and asserts p99 < configured threshold. 3) Full mixed-tenant nightly job that records artifacts to /artifacts/pulseweave/<date>. 4) Customer acceptance checklist runbook that an SRE can execute with a customer during onboarding. 5) Canary experiment: run Pulseweave against 10% of fleet capacity for a canary model variant and validate fallback behavior.
telemetry_requirements: Prometheus metrics: pulseweave.run_id, request.type, tenant.bucket, seq_length, token_latencies_histogram, request_latency_ms, error_count
Tracing: request id -> node id -> kernel op spans (to correlate kernel stalls)
Autoscaler events: node_add, node_remove, scale_reason, scale_duration
Artifact outputs: evidence_bundle.json, telemetry_timeseries.csv, docker-compose-equivalent manifest for local repro
operational_playbook: Run commands: ./bin/pulseweave run --manifest manifests/mixed-tenant.yaml --seed 1234 --out artifacts/2025-03-20; Inspect artifacts: ./tools/plot-evidence artifacts/2025-03-20/evidence_bundle.json; To rerun with autoscaler perturbation: ./bin/pulseweave run --manifest manifests/surge-burst.yaml --simulate-autoscaler-delay 45s. Playbook includes troubleshooting section for: (a) persistent high p99 tied to KV misses; (b) sustained error spikes due to node OOMs; (c) autoscaler flapping during ramp (recommended throttle window adjustments).
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal alpha — limited to QA cluster and SRE (2 weeks). Phase 2: beta — run nightly on staging against fleet-simulator infra and collect 10 golden runs (4 weeks). Phase 3: customer pilots — run with two early customers during onboarding and produce acceptance artifacts (2-6 weeks). Post-pilot: incorporate feedback and flip default acceptance script in the onboarding docs.
deliverables: console integration for attaching acceptance bundles to customer accounts
observability_artifacts: Grafana dashboards: Pulseweave > Throughput Signature, Pulseweave > Autoscaler Events, Pulseweave > Kernel Stall Correlation. Example links: https://grafana.internal.redwood/pulseweave-throughput (alpha), https://console.redwood.internal/acceptance/ENG-100500 (acceptance artifacts placeholder).
security_considerations: All request templates are sanitized and PII-free. Evidence bundles are stored in a restricted GCS bucket with customer-specific ACLs when used for onboarding. CI artifacts are ephemeral and redacted. No production keys are used in synthetic runs. Any real-customer trace ingestion must be opt-in and scrubbed per compliance rules.
dependencies_notes: Requires: updates to autoscaler metrics exporter (ENG-30721) to surface scale_reason; small runtime shim to emit kernel-op spans (runtime-1.20 change); console API endpoint to attach acceptance bundles to a customer object.
notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on the measurement and evidence side of throughput guarantees rather than the legal contract text. Legal/Sales alignment to use these artifacts in customer-facing SLA/acceptance will be a follow-up with Documentation and Sales Ops.
next_steps: 1) Spike: build minimal driver and run single mixed-tenant profile in QA (owner: Marco Liu, 3d). 2) Instrument evidence collector and wire Prometheus metrics (owner: Aisha Patel, 4d). 3) Draft runbook and acceptance checklist, coordinate with Sales for pilot customers (owner: Product Ops).
